_meta.description: Golden-truth Reddit-style comments for buzz classifier eval. Each case targets a specific decision boundary documented in the classifier prompt (scripts/lib/buzz-classifier.js). Hand-labeled 2026-04-15 based on the prompt's own YES/NO enumerated rules.
_meta.labelingNotes: Label reflects what the prompt EXPLICITLY instructs. If a case fails, either the LLM is wrong OR the prompt is ambiguous — treat failures as prompt-improvement opportunities.

cases.body: Saw Wicked last night and it was absolutely incredible. Cynthia's voice is otherworldly.
cases.rationale: past-tense attendance + superlative

cases.body: Going to see Wicked tomorrow, so excited!
cases.rationale: future tense — prompt: 'planning to see it' = NOT relevant

cases.body: I refuse to see Wicked until Cynthia apologizes for her comments.
cases.rationale: boycott sentiment, did not attend

cases.body: Hamilton is way better than Wicked, it's not even close.
cases.rationale: comment references a different show by name

cases.body: I saw it opening week and felt underwhelmed. The second act dragged.
cases.rationale: attended, negative verdict — 'the second act dragged' is negative

cases.body: The book this is based on is terrible so I'm skipping the show.
cases.rationale: opinion about source material, not the production; did not attend

cases.body: Saw it twice already, taking my mom next month.
cases.rationale: 'saw it twice' + returning = implicit positive per prompt guidance

cases.body: Loved the performances but the story didn't really work for me.
cases.rationale: both positive and negative aspects explicitly in same comment

cases.body: The ushers at the Gershwin were so rude, worst theater experience.
cases.rationale: venue/logistics/usher behavior — about the venue, not the show

cases.body: My partner and I saw it in May and we were completely blown away.
cases.rationale: past attendance + 'blown away' = enthusiastic

cases.body: The show opens April 3rd and runs through September.
cases.rationale: meta/scheduling discussion, no audience reaction

cases.body: We saw it last week. Glad I went but I don't think I'd pay full price again.
cases.rationale: attended, positive ('glad I went') AND negative ('wouldn't pay full price') = mixed

cases.body: Heard the lead was out this week due to illness.
cases.rationale: industry talk — cast illness/contracts, not an audience reaction

cases.body: 10/10 absolutely life-changing experience, everyone needs to see this.
cases.rationale: implied attendance + '10/10' + 'life-changing' = enthusiastic

cases.body: I've heard it's pretty good but haven't seen it myself.
cases.rationale: did not attend ('haven't seen it myself')

cases.body: Tickets are insanely expensive now, might wait for the tour.
cases.rationale: meta discussion about ticket prices, not an audience reaction

cases.body: Saw it last night. It was fine. Not sure why everyone raves about it.
cases.rationale: attended + 'fine' + undercutting hype = negative verdict disguised as lukewarm

cases.body: My kids came home from the matinee yesterday singing Defying Gravity all night. They loved it.
cases.rationale: second-hand but clear attendance + 'loved it' = positive

cases.body: About to head into the theater now, reporting back after!
cases.rationale: pre-show, has not yet attended

cases.body: Saw it Saturday. The spectacle was incredible but the pacing was rough in act 2.
cases.rationale: attended, explicit both ('spectacle incredible', 'pacing rough') = mixed
